findings.reason: package.json:21-29 lists only bin, range.bnf, classes, functions, internal, ranges and index.js. The diff adds preload.js at the root but doesn't change "files", so npm publish won't ship it.
findings.claim: preload.js is missing from the package.json "files" allowlist, so the published package leaves it out and require('semver/preload') fails for anyone who installs it.
findings.evidence: The diff adds only `preload.js` at the repo root. package.json's "files" whitelist is ["bin", "range.bnf", "classes", "functions", "internal", "ranges", "index.js"], with no "preload.js" entry. npm publishes only whitelisted paths plus package.json, README and LICENSE.

findings.reason: test/preload.js:2 requires '../preload.js' directly and only compares it with index. Nothing checks the "files" list or npm pack output, so the suite passes even with the packaging defect.
findings.claim: The test loads preload.js from the source tree, so it can't catch the file being left out of the published package.
findings.evidence: test/preload.js does `require('../preload.js')` and `t.strictSame(preload, index, ...)`. Nothing exercises `npm pack` output or the package's "files" list.

findings.reason: A search of the export finds 'preload' only in test/preload.js. README.md and CHANGELOG.md don't mention it. With no story.md in the packet, I can't tell whether docs were in scope.
findings.claim: The new public entry point semver/preload is not documented in README or CHANGELOG.
findings.evidence: A search for 'preload' outside test/ finds nothing in README.md or CHANGELOG.md. The only explanation is the comment on preload.js line 1: "just pre-load all the stuff that index.js lazily exports".
